claim: The NETFRAMEWORK half of every new preprocessor guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage even on supported .NET Framework targets where System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists (it has been available since .NET Framework 4.0). Consequently, generated code for targets such as net472 remains included in coverage, although the requirement calls for conditional omission only where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageNetFrameworkRequirementsTests.GeneratedTypesAreDecoratedOnNetFramework. It generates and compiles the output against the .NET Framework 4.7.2 reference assemblies with NETFRAMEWORK defined, then asserts that every generated type has an active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. The current guards make all such attributes inactive, so the test fails on head.

claim: The framework guards suppress the attribute on .NET Standard 2.0 and every .NET Framework target, even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on those frameworks. Generated code for those supported targets therefore remains undecorated, contrary to the unconditional coverage requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTemplateEdgeTests.NetStandard20GeneratedTypesAreDecorated: generate formatter and resolver sources, parse them with NETSTANDARD2_0 defined, and verify every generated class has ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The guarded attribute fragments are inactive, so the test fails on head.

claim: Adding ExcludeFromCodeCoverage to the generated half of a user-declared partial resolver produces CS0579 when the user has already applied the same non-repeatable attribute to that resolver. Previously valid source no longer compiles.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTemplateEdgeTests.UserAttributedPartialResolverStillCompiles. It declares a GeneratedMessagePackResolver partial class that already has ExcludeFromCodeCoverage; compilation succeeds on base and reports duplicate-attribute CS0579 on head.

claim: The new tests never compile the generated output or assert generator diagnostics. They can pass when the added attribute/directives make the generated source invalid, and they do not actually verify the acceptance criterion that generation compiles for NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK; matching the expected guard text is not equivalent to compiling with those symbols.

receipt_plan.detail: Extend RunGeneratorAsync or add tests that retain the updated compilation and assert no generator or compilation diagnostics. Parse/run the generated sources once with no target symbols and again with NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK defined, using corresponding framework references, and assert successful compilation and that the attribute is absent on those targets.
